newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Shell Sri Lanka strike to continue.
newsitem.headline: Shell Sri Lanka strike to continue.

text.p: Talks to end a three-day strike at Sri Lanka's monopoly gas distributor, owned by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, which has crippled distribution, ended inconclusively on Monday, the Labour Commissioner said.
"It looks like the strike will continue as the two sides could not reach agreement on the main issues," R. Wimalasena told Reuters. "However, I hope to arrange another round of talks."

The strike was launched on Friday by workers of the All Ceylon Commercial and Industrial Workers Union demanding an immediate halt to transfers of employees and the reinstatement of six workers who were dismissed.
Wimalasena mediated between the labour union and company officials to try to end the strike.
The spokesman for Shell Gas Lanka was not immediately available for comment.

The company spokesman said earlier that their two main plants near Colombo had stopped supplying gas but two centres in southern Galle and Kandy, in the central hills, were still filling cylinders of consumers.

"The supply situation is pretty critical," the spokesman said. "We're beginning to get a situation where a lot of dealers do not have stocks and there's severe pressure from industrial users who have very low stock levels."
A ship with 1,750 tonnes of gas has been waiting outside Colombo port since Saturday, unable to unload because of the strike, he also said.
This is the second strike at the company since it was privatised in October 1995.

A six-day strike by union labour, demanding the reinstatement of nine workers suspended for violating safety rules at Colombo port when unloading gas, brought gas distribution to a halt in the Indian Ocean island last November.
